analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md, with two edits. Head line 324 changes the dense Qwen plain-chunk size under decode company from 512 to 2,048. Head lines 534-540 add a note that 2,048-token plain chunks leave no durable boundary in prompts shorter than 2,048 tokens, and that the deepest boundary at or below a hint can sit up to 2,047 tokens below it. The note cites EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift `usesWidePrefillChunk`. No code, configuration, crypto, scoping, TTL, KEK, HMAC naming or routing logic is modified. I found no change to the T-041 mitigations: the encrypted DBK3 at-rest files, HMAC lookup tags, account/model cacheSalt scoping, the 30-minute TTL, the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE switch, or the SEC-035 accepted risk.

The documented behavior is a reduction in durable checkpoint granularity, which means fewer SSD donations and less at-rest surface. It is a performance and cache-hit effect, not a security regression. A coarser checkpoint boundary could marginally shift the same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035) by making hits rarer. That is already accepted and not materially altered.

The underlying code change that `usesWidePrefillChunk` describes is not in the supplied evidence. The doc claims it exists, but I could not verify it. A later pass should check that the code change keeps the 256-token alignment and the 1,024-token floor, and does not alter packed-prefill disarm or the SSD identity/cacheSalt binding. This is an unverified contract, not a finding, because the PR adds no code here.
